The **2019 Tour de Wallonie** was the **46th edition** of this annual road cycling stage race held in the Wallonia region of Belgium. Here’s a comprehensive breakdown of everything you need to know about the race:

---

### **📅 Key Details**
- **Dates:** July 27 – July 31, 2019
- **Edition:** 46th
- **Race Type:** Men’s professional stage race (UCI Europe Tour, Category **2.HC**)
- **Organizer:** ASO (Amaury Sport Organisation)
- **Location:** Wallonia, Belgium
- **Total Distance:** ~680 km (across 5 stages)

---

### **🏆 Race Overview**
The **Tour de Wallonie** is a mid-season stage race often used by riders as preparation for the **Ardennes Classics** (like Liège-Bastogne-Liège) or the **Vuelta a España**. The 2019 edition featured a mix of **hilly and flat stages**, with a **time trial** and a **mountainous finish** on the final day.

---

### **📌 Stages & Results**
The race consisted of **5 stages**:

#### **🥇 Stage 1: July 27 – Charleroi > Charleroi (186.7 km)**
- **Type:** Flat stage (slightly rolling)
- **Winner:** **Caleb Ewan** (Lotto-Soudal) – *Mass sprint finish*
- **Key Moments:**
  - Early breakaway by **Ludos De Winter (Wanty-Gobert)** and **Julien Van den Brande (Sport Vlaanderen-Baloise)**.
  - Ewan outsprinted **Christopher Lawless (Ineos Grenadiers)** and **Sacha Modolo (EF Education First)**.

#### **🥈 Stage 2: July 28 – Verviers > Pépinster (152.9 km)**
- **Type:** Hilly stage
- **Winner:** **्डLoic Vliegen** (Wanty-Gobert)
- **Key Moments:**
  - **Solo attack** in the final kilometers after a breakaway with **Bjorg Lambrecht (Lotto-Soudal)**.
  - Vliegen held off the peloton by **7 seconds**.
  - **Marcel Meisen (Corendon-Circus)** took 2nd, **Lawless** 3rd.

#### **🥉 Stage 3: July 29 – Visé > Thuin (176.2 km)**
- **Type:** Rolling stage with steep climbs
- **Winner:** **Greg Van Avermaet** (CCC Team)
- **Key Moments:**
  - **Hilly finish** with a **cobblestone climb** near the end.
  - Van Avermaet attacked in the final kilometer, dropping **Lawless** and **Diego Ulissi (UAE Emirates)**.
  - **1st GC shakeup** – **Lawless took the leader’s jersey**.

#### **4️⃣ Stage 4: July 30 – Profondeville > Tinne (15.2 km, Individual Time Trial)**
- **Type:** Flat to rolling ITT
- **Winner:** **Yves Lampaert** (Deceuninck-Quick Step) – *Dominated with a 17:50 time*
- **Key Moments:**
  - **Lawless** retained the lead but lost **12 seconds** to ** têtes Ulissi**.
  - **Bob Jungels (Deceuninck-Quick Step)** finished 2nd, **Stefan Küng (Groupama-FDJ)** 3rd.
- **GC Standings After Stage 4:**
  1. **Christopher Lawless** (Ineos Grenadiers) – **12:52:54**
  2. Diego Ulissi (UAE Emirates) – **+0:10**
  3. James Knox (Deceuninck-Quick Step) – **+0:25**

#### **5️⃣ Stage 5: July 31 – Mont-de-l'Enclus > mur de Thuin (184.5 km)**
- **Type:** **Mountainous stage** (King of the Mountains classification decisive)
- **Winner:** **Loïc Vliegen** (Wanty-Gobert) – *Second stage win*
- **Key Moments:**
  - **Final showdown** on the **Mur de Thuin** (a **23.6% gradient** cobblestone climb).
  - **ULissI and Lawless** attacked on the final climb, but **Vliegen countered** to take the stage.
  - **Lawless held on for 2nd**, securing the **overall victory**.
- **Final GC Podium:**
  1. **🇬🇧 Christopher Lawless** (Ineos Grenadiers) – **17:05:36**
  2. **🇮🇹 Diego Ulissi** (UAE Emirates) – **+0:10**
  3. **🇬🇧 James Knox** (Deceuninck-Quick Step) – **+0:25**

---

### **🏆 Final Classifications**
| **Classification** | **Winner** | **Team** | **Points/Time** |
|---------------------|------------|----------|----------------|
| **General (GC)** | Christopher Lawless | Ineos Grenadiers | 17:05:36 |
| **Points** | Greg Van Avermaet | CCC Team | 49 pts |
| **Mountains (KOM)** | Loïc Vliegen | Wanty-Gobert | 44 pts |
| **Best Young Rider** | James Knox | Deceuninck-Quick Step | 17:05:61 |
| **Teams** | Deceuninck-Quick Step | - | - |

---

### **🔍 Key Takeaways & Highlights**
✅ **Christopher Lawless’ Breakthrough**
- First **major stage race victory** of his career.
- Proved his **climbing and time-trial abilities** (finished 2nd in the ITT).

✅ **Loïc Vliegen’s Double Stage Win**
- Won **Stage 2 (solo attack)** and **Stage 5 (Mur de Thuin)**.
- Strong **hilly terrain specialist**.

✅ **Greg Van Avermaet’s Form**
- Showed **classics-like strength** with his Stage 3 win.
- Took the **points jersey**.

✅ **Diego Ulissi’s Consistency**
- **2nd overall** (only **10 seconds behind Lawless**).
- Strong **all-rounder performance**.

✅ **Yves Lampaert’s TT Dominance**
- Won the **individual time trial** by a **huge margin (24 sec)**.

✅ **Tragedy in the Race**
- **Bjorg Lambrecht** (Lotto-Soudal), who was in the **breakaway on Stage 2**, tragically **died in a crash during the 2019 Tour de Pologne** just weeks later.

---

### **📺 TV & Coverage**
- The race was **broadcast live** on **RTBF (Belgian TV)** and **Eurosport**.
- Highlights available on **YouTube (UCI & team channels)**.

---
---
### **💬 Notable Quotes**
- **Christopher Lawless (After Winning):**
  *"It’s incredible. I came here to test myself, and to win is a dream. The team supported me perfectly."*
- **Loïc Vliegen (After Stage 5 Win):**
  *"The Mur de Thuin is brutal, but I had the legs today. To win twice in this race is special."*

---
---
### **📊 Race Statistics**
- **Average Speed (Winner’s): ~42.5 km/h** (Lawless)
- **Total Prize Money:** ~€100,000
- **Number of Teams:** **20 teams** (WorldTeams, ProTeams, Continental)
- **Start List Highlights:**
  - **Greg Van Avermaet (CCC)**
  - **Diego Ulissi (UAE)**
  - **Yves Lampaert (Deceuninck-Quick Step)**
  - **Bob Jungels (Deceuninck-Quick Step)**
  - **Once... Caleb Ewan (Lotto-Soudal)**

---
---
### **🔗 External Links (For More Info)**
- [ProCyclingStats – 2019 Tour de Wallonie](https://www.procyclingstats.com/race/tour-de-wallonie/2019)
- [Official Race Website (Archive)](https://www.tourdewallonie.be/)
- [Cycling Archives – Results](https://www.cyclingarchives.com/race.php?raceid=44156)

---
---
### **🏁 Legacy & Impact**
- **Lawless’ win** marked him as a **future Grand Tour contender** (later rode in the **2020 Giro d’Italia**).
- **Van Avermaet’s victory** reinforced his **classics specialist status**.
- The **Mur de Thuin** finale became a **signature finish** for the race in later editions.
